findings.message: 19.P3.admission-holds-activation requires build_daemon_core to construct one consumer with build_control and also refuse an absent consumer. Its Tests bullet requires that refusal while leaving CoreRig unchanged; CoreRig supplies a Checkout without control. Refusing absent input breaks CoreRig, while constructing the consumer makes the specified absence refusal unreachable. This contradiction also exists on the base commit.
findings.paved_road: Harden 19.P3.admission-holds-activation under section 11.4 to choose one construction rule. Either retain build_daemon_core as the consumer construction root and remove its absent-consumer refusal and test obligation, or require caller-supplied Checkout.control and explicitly require CoreRig migration. Then regenerate phase3-continue-09, including its verbatim contract block; preserve the approved phase3-continue-10 seed byte-identically.
